hyperedges.label: Two-Tier Hybrid Rendering in One Dispatch

nodes.label: RayTracer Solution Map
nodes.rationale: Splits into RayTracer.Core (engine), RayTracer.Gpu (single WinForms/DXR app + CPU renderer), RayTracer.Tests, Benchmark, and .net tooling project.

nodes.label: Render Data Flow Pipeline
nodes.rationale: Seven ordered stages: BVH build -> JobSystem tile scheduling -> PathTracer -> AccumulationBuffer -> TaaResolver -> DisplayResolver (XYZ->sRGB) -> optional DebugBufferRenderer.

nodes.label: Engine Design Intent (thin facade, focused hot loops)
nodes.rationale: Keep JobSystem a thin orchestration facade; keep hot loops in focused components for profiling; prefer deterministic tests around resolve/accumulation/color conversion.
nodes.norm_label: engine design intent (thin facade, focused hot loops)

nodes.label: Renderer Debug Options Plan (F1-F10)
nodes.rationale: Beauty on F1, debug screens F2-F8, F9/F10 toggle overlay; instrument accumulation with per-sample metadata (bounce, clamp, reuse, timestamp) and keep debug modes off by default to limit overhead.

nodes.norm_label: raytracer remaining work (single source of truth)

nodes.label: Engine Working Conventions (CPU->reference->HLSL)
nodes.rationale: Land in RayTracer.Core CPU first, port to pure-C# *Reference.cs (the CI contract since CI has no GPU), then HLSL line-for-line; keep the no-effect path byte-identical (goldens unmoved); spectral-native color from physics; gate on cost via presets leaning on accumulation/TAA.

nodes.label: Spectral / Optical Effects (mirror, dielectric, dispersion, thin-film, Beer-Lambert)
nodes.norm_label: spectral / optical effects (mirror, dielectric, dispersion, thin-film, beer-lambert)

nodes.label: Camera Lens Models (pinhole/phone/simple/cine)
nodes.rationale: Physical thin-lens ray gen in metres so f/N gives photographic DoF; pinhole is default and bit-exact (draws no random numbers, own RNG stream via LensSampler.SeedFor).

nodes.label: Space Cadet RT Vision (spectral ray-traced pinball)
nodes.rationale: Fixed camera means the static playfield can be rendered by the full Phase 6 spectral path and converge over many frames to near-offline look at real-time cost; pinball is the mirror image of the maze (static scene, moving camera vs static camera, few moving parts).
nodes.norm_label: space cadet rt vision (spectral ray-traced pinball)

nodes.label: Pinball Design Pillars & Non-goals
nodes.rationale: Faithful to the Windows table (no multiball, Replay free balls); reuse the engine don't fork; static playfield = full RT, movers = cheap tier; spectral-native color; gate on cost via Classic/RT-Showcase presets; determinism; physics fidelity is a first-class pillar where realism wins over 1995 feel.

nodes.label: Hybrid Rendering Within One DXR Dispatch
nodes.norm_label: hybrid rendering within one dxr dispatch

nodes.label: Phase 6 is One Dispatch, Not a G-buffer Compositor
nodes.rationale: Phase6Renderer.RenderFrame records exactly one inline DXR 1.1 trace as a compute shader against one Scene TLAS; there is no rasterizer/G-buffer, so 'static vs moving' is a per-primitive shading budget inside ShadeSample, not a separate pass. Occlusion, ball reflection and contact shadow fall out of the single TLAS.
nodes.norm_label: phase 6 is one dispatch, not a g-buffer compositor

nodes.label: Static Playfield Tier (full spectral, converged)
nodes.rationale: Fixed/slow camera lets AccumulationBuffer + TaaResolver converge these pixels to high effective spp; an insert/light change must NOT route through _forceReset (throws away indirect convergence) but use an in-place short-window reconverge.

nodes.label: Dynamic Tier (cheap single-bounce hero/RGB movers)
nodes.rationale: Movers are deliberately NOT spectral path traced: fast movers break temporal reuse (a ball crosses a pixel in 2-3 frames), so they ride a bounded MotionSampleCap window with single-bounce direct shading, generalizing the shipped isMover path.

nodes.label: Hit-id Restart (the ghost-trail fix)
nodes.rationale: The per-pixel restart uses a 1-bit hit/miss mask, so a fast ball sliding off a pixel lets the ramp behind blend into the ball's stale mean; storing a dynamic-vs-static id and restarting on id change forces a clean 1-sample restart.

nodes.label: pathTouchedDynamic Flag (ball ghost in static specular)
nodes.norm_label: pathtoucheddynamic flag (ball ghost in static specular)

nodes.label: Chrome Ball Money Shots (mirror + contact shadow)
nodes.rationale: Both already shipped: mirror reflection via TraceSpecularRadiance into the static TLAS (cap to 1 bounce, hero-only ideal for neutral chrome); hard contact shadow free because an opaque sphere commits as an occluder in TraceTransmittance's candidate loop.
nodes.norm_label: chrome ball money shots (mirror + contact shadow)

nodes.label: Emissive-Surface Shading (new, largest renderer add)
nodes.rationale: SurfaceKind.Emissive exists only as an enum with no tracer term (emissive AOV is literally zero); neon inserts/wormholes/bumper-pops need an emission term in ShadeSample's diffuse terminal, the indirect bounce and as an NEE emitter. Prerequisite for P0 to look right.

nodes.label: RTX 3070 Performance Budget & Presets
nodes.rationale: The real cost is the per-frame AS refit stalls (fold into the trace command list, keep the TLAS UAV barrier, drop the redundant WaitForGpu), not ray throughput; caustics/photon map stay off the frame budget (built once at table load).

nodes.label: Trajectory Comes From Physics (governing principle)
nodes.rationale: The exact analogue of 'color comes from spectral physics, never a hard-coded tint': trajectory comes from gravity/inertia/friction/restitution/spin/drag in measured SI units, never a feel-tweak; validated by fixed-seed unit tests against closed-form results, realism wins over 1995 feel.

nodes.label: 6-DOF Ball Rigid-Body Model (double precision)
nodes.rationale: Full 3-D gravity applied to the body against a tilted playfield collider (not pre-projected slope accel), so the ball naturally climbs ramps, goes airborne and lands with no special-casing; solid-sphere isotropic inertia makes I-inverse just 1/I.

nodes.label: Analytic Collider Zoo (Plane/Sphere/Cylinder/Capsule/Quad/Arc/Mesh)
nodes.rationale: Every sphere-vs-X closest-feature query is closed-form; broadphase reuses the existing float BVH conservatively while narrowphase/integration run in double.

nodes.label: Restitution + Coulomb-Friction Impulse Solver
nodes.rationale: Normal impulse is torque-free (passes through sphere centre) so bounces never create spin; all spin comes from the tangential friction impulse capped by the Coulomb cone with tangential reduced mass 2m/7; grip vs slide emerges from j_t* vs mu*j_n.

nodes.label: Spin, Magnus & Rebound-Angle Coupling
nodes.rationale: Spin is generated only through the tangential friction impulse; it changes outgoing angle via tangential coupling (backspin/topspin/sidespin alter rebound). Magnus is implemented physically correctly but is honestly tiny (a few mm) for a dense steel ball.

nodes.label: Aerodynamic Drag & Rolling Resistance
nodes.rationale: Quadratic drag is negligible at pinball speed (terminal velocity ~70 m/s) but included for correctness; rolling resistance is the dominant non-Coulomb loss that shapes pacing (how far a slow ball coasts).

nodes.label: Fixed-Timestep Symplectic Euler + CCD (1000 Hz)
nodes.rationale: Symplectic Euler over RK4 because it doesn't pump energy into resting contact; CCD is mandatory because a 5-10 m/s ball moves 5-10 mm/step and would tunnel thin walls; swept-sphere conservative advancement reuses the BVH broadphase; determinism via fixed h, fixed contact order, double, seeded PRNG.

nodes.label: Actuators (flippers, plunger, bumpers, nudge/tilt)
nodes.rationale: Flippers are kinematic torque-limited capsules whose surface velocity u=omega x r transfers push+spin (the skill mechanic emerges, unscripted); bumpers/slingshots are the one place energy is added via a measured coil impulse; nudge impulses the ball and shifts the table frame with a tilt-bob leaky integrator.

nodes.label: Build vs Buy: Custom Analytic Solver
nodes.rationale: One dynamic ball + static world + few kinematic actuators makes an exact analytic single-sphere solver viable; custom wins on physical control, closed-form-testable determinism and fit; BepuPhysics v2 is the pure-C# fallback if scope grows to multi-ball; keep PhysicsWorld swappable behind an interface.
nodes.norm_label: build vs buy: custom analytic solver

nodes.label: Engine <-> Maze Separation (Milestone E)
nodes.rationale: Break three RayTracer.Core maze leaks (CameraController->MazeNavigator dependency, MazeGeometryBuilder.CellSize world-scale constant, LensOptions doc comment) and split RayTracer.Gpu into a reusable backend + a new RayTracer.Maze app; acceptance is a pure move-and-reparameterize with goldens unmoved.

nodes.label: CI Build-Test Workflow (.NET 10, windows-latest)
nodes.rationale: Restore/build/test .net.csproj in Release, an analyzer-checks build with RunAnalyzers=true, and an optional benchmark run gated behind workflow_dispatch.

nodes.label: No-Nullables / Explicit-Usings Convention
nodes.rationale: Avoid nullables (use Result<T> or remove the ? annotations rather than #nullable enable); all enums have an empty value; implicit usings are disabled so all System.* usings are explicit in GlobalUsings.cs.
